name: Stormshell Parka
description: Hooded rain parka with taped seams. Rain beads up and runs off.
wash: Machine wash at 30°C. The finish wears off over time.
afterwards: PFAS don't break down. They stay in water and soil after the jacket is thrown away.
altName: The same parka with a PFAS-free finish
altNote: Wax or silicone-based repellents work for everyday rain. In heavy storms, fluorinated finishes tend to do better.

name: Trail Sneaker
description: Waterproof sneaker for wet streets and muddy parks.
wash: Wipe clean only. Do not machine wash.
afterwards: Scuffing and cleaning can release bits of the coating into dust and rinse water.
altNote: Natural wax proofing keeps shoes dry in the city and can be reapplied at home.

name: Stainguard Chino
description: Chino that shrugs off coffee. Spills bead up and roll off.
wash: Machine wash at 40°C. Part of the finish goes down the drain with every wash.
afterwards: Treatment plants don't filter out PFAS well, so they pass through to rivers and the sea.
altName: Untreated cotton, or silica or polyurethane-based treatments
altNote: Untreated, tightly woven cotton is easier to clean than most people expect. Silica and polyurethane treatments give some stain resistance without PFAS.

name: Drizzle Bucket Hat
description: Bucket hat with a wide brim. Keeps rain off your face.
afterwards: Same finish as the parka, just on a smaller item.
altNote: Waxed cotton repels water without fluorinated chemicals. It also gets better looking with age.

name: Wax
description: Glide wax for the base of your skis. Faster on the piste.
content: Paraffin wax with a fluorinated additive
wash: Rubbed or ironed into the ski base. It wears off on the snow while you ski.
afterwards: The wax that wears off stays on the snow. Fluorinated additives don't break down and can end up in meltwater and soil.
altNote: Fluorine-free waxes work for everyday skiing. They can be a bit slower in some snow.

name: Gloves
description: Insulated ski gloves that keep out wet snow.
wash: Hand wash at 30°C. The finish wears off over time.
afterwards: Washing sends part of the finish into the wastewater, and PFAS pass through treatment plants.
altNote: Wax or silicone-based finishes keep out wet snow, but you may need to reapply them more often.
